title: Year-Round Property Maintenance Guide for Simcoe County Homeowners
seoTitle: Simcoe County Property Maintenance Guide by Season
seoDescription: A seasonal maintenance schedule for homeowners in Barrie, Collingwood, Wasaga Beach and the Georgian Bay region.
html:
Property maintenance in Simcoe County follows the seasons. The climate brings hard winters, wet springs, hot humid summers and fast-changing shoulder seasons. Each season has its own priorities. Staying ahead of the calendar keeps small upkeep from turning into larger reactive repairs. When a task is beyond your own time or tools, send a request through Collingwood Handyman with photos and your address. A local service provider can review the request and confirm whether the job is within scope.

Spring (March to May): Recovery and Inspection

Spring is inspection season. After months of freeze-thaw cycles and heavy snow loads, walk the entire property. Look for frost heaving in walkways, cracks in foundations and driveways, and damage to exterior cladding or roofing. Clean eavestroughs before spring rains begin. Blocked gutters in spring are a common cause of water problems around foundations.

Service the lawn irrigation system if you have one. Inspect all outdoor taps and hose bibs after the final freeze to confirm they were not damaged. Check the sump pump. Spring is its busiest season, and a failed pump during snowmelt can lead to serious water damage. For cottage and seasonal property owners, the cottage opening checklist covers the extra spring tasks for properties left vacant through winter.

Summer (June to August): Surface Work and Protecting Assets

Summer is the best window for exterior painting, deck refinishing, sealing concrete and above-grade exterior work. Warm, dry weather means faster drying times and better product performance. Plan exterior work early, since local schedules fill quickly through July and August. A pressure washing session at the start of summer is often the first step before painting or staining.

Trim vegetation back from the house. Shrubs and trees against the exterior hold moisture and give pests a path inside. Keep at least 15 to 20 cm of clearance between plants and the siding or foundation.

Fall (September to November): Prepare and Protect

Fall is the most important season for preventive maintenance in this region. Service the heating system before you need it. Replace furnace filters and have the furnace inspected, especially an older unit. Test carbon monoxide and smoke detectors and replace batteries. For cottage owners, the cottage closing checklist walks through the tasks specific to seasonal properties.

Seal exterior gaps that pests could use to overwinter inside. Mice and red squirrels are persistent in fall. Walk the perimeter and look for gaps at pipe penetrations, vents, fascia joints and foundation sills. An hour of prevention here is well spent.

Disconnect and drain garden hoses. Blow out irrigation systems. Stack and cover outdoor furniture. Apply a protective sealant to concrete driveways and walkways before freeze season to reduce salt and frost damage.

Winter (December to February): Monitor and Prevent Ice Damage

Ice damming is the main winter risk for roofs in this region. Poor attic insulation and ventilation let heat escape through the roof. The heat melts snow, which refreezes at the cold eaves and forms ice dams. Water backs up behind the dam and gets under shingles. If you have had ice damming, improving attic insulation is the correct long-term fix.

Check the roof after heavy snowfalls. Roofs are designed for snow load, but wet, heavy snow after a rain event can exceed load limits, especially on older structures or low-pitch roofs. A roof rake used from the ground can reduce the load without the risk of climbing a ladder in winter conditions.

Getting help with seasonal tasks

If you would rather hand off part of this schedule, send a request through Collingwood Handyman. List the tasks, the property address, whether the home is occupied year-round, and any access details. A local service provider can review the request and confirm which tasks are within scope. Ask for an itemized written quote, and ask about insurance and timing before work starts. Furnace, gas, electrical and roofing work belong with the appropriate licensed trade.
